reviews.title: A sleek and capable rig for gaming on the go
reviews.content:
The MSI Stealth 16 AI+ has been very close to the perfect laptop for me. The OLED is the headline, 2.5K at a variable 240Hz, and it somehow still manages stellar battery life, which isn't a sentence I expected to write about a gaming laptop. The bezels are tiny so the footprint is smaller than a 16 inch spec sheet suggests, and between that and the weight it ends up far more portable than you'd expect. The branding is minimal and tasteful on the gunmetal/graphite chassis, and it's thin relative to most gaming machines but still well appointed in both compute capability and connectivity.

On that note: a proprietary power connector (though the Type-C ports do support power delivery), 2 x Thunderbolt 4, 2 x USB 3.2 Gen 2 Type A, headphone jack, HDMI, and most critically in my opinion, a 2.5G ethernet port. I'd rather be hardwired whenever I have the option, so that last one carries more weight for me than it probably does for most people.

The keyboard is really comfortable and easy to type on and I had no issues adapting to it. The 4 zone RGB is a little odd, it would have been nice for the keys to have individual lighting especially at this price point, but it's not something I think about while I'm actually using the machine. I didn't really care about the lack of a number pad and I prefer the trade-off for proper speaker grilles. The audio quality is surprisingly good given the size of the laptop. The trackpad is giant and responsive, I still wouldn't game on it, but I think you actually could if you wanted to.

The camera is average, but you probably aren't buying this laptop for the camera. WiFi performed well with strong download speeds in my testing. Graphics wise the Stealth is no slouch either, I managed a respectable 2550 in 3DMark, and that number lines up with how the games I've played actually feel.

For the mix of work and gaming I do, this is the closest thing I've used to the right machine.

reviews.title: Excellent high end laptop
reviews.content:
I was eager to try out this new MSI Stealth 16” Gaming Laptop and it did not disappoint.

Pros:
Big bright 2560x1600 OLED display
NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 graphics
Intel® Core™ Ultra 9-386H Processor
32GB DDR5 5600MHZ RAM
1 TB SSD
Better than expected audio
Lots of ports including Ethernet
Cool RGB Keyboard lights
Light for a big laptop
Respectable benchmark scores for a gaming laptop

Cons:
Proprietary charging port
No number pad
Pricey

The first thing I noticed is the big bright screen on this laptop. The OLED screen is impressive. Note that this laptop, as with most gaming laptops, is not Touchscreen capable. There is an extra-large touchpad that makes navigation easy. The second thing I noticed is the selection of ports. Two USB Type A, two USB-C/Thunderbolt 5, Ethernet/LAN port, HDMI port and a proprietary charging port. Ample ports to use this system without a docking station. 

I ran both PassMark and 3Dmark benchmarking tests. First round of benchmarking was disappointing. But I ran them again the second day and found them much improved. I suspect I ran the first round too soon after initial setup, since I hadn’t changed any settings. Second round of benchmark scores include: 
PassMark Overall Rating - 11812.6 (88th Percentile)
3Dmark CPU Profile score - Max threads 9325
3Dmark Speed Way Score - 2785 
3Dmark Steel Nomad Score – 2399 (DX12)

Next, I fired up a couple of games. Game play was smooth and the system was responsive. The graphics were great and the sound was surprisingly good for laptop built-in speakers. 

Overall, I was impressed with this laptop. The screen is big and bright, the audio is very good, RAM and storage are good, although more RAM would be better. It is responsive, even though I do miss the number keypad. If you are a PC gamer, looking for a laptop that you can use for work and gaming, this one is worth a look.

reviews.title: Capable of being a work AND gaming laptop
reviews.content:
I love playing Fortnite with my friends, which is almost always random availability. I used to quickly turn on the PS5 and play, but PS5 is now a bit "slow" due to the aging hardware - anyone with a better computer can easily overtake me as I'm the one lagging. I can get around this with my iPad Pro M5, but it also means rearranging my desk to push my laptop aside to feature my iPad. It works, but with limited space, it's a bit of an annoyance. I've had/have several laptops, each with their own purpose, but my gaming laptops are now old, and can't handle Fortnite without dropping the visual qualities, and that's not fun when you record the sessions. 

Enter MSI's Stealth 16 AI! It has 32GB of RAM, a 1TB nvme, and most importantly a dedicated NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060. Outside of it missing a touch screen and a numeric keypad, the laptop can easily serve as a main/work computer. 

Visually, the first things you'll notice is the rather large touchpad and the colorfully lit keys. By default they cycle through all the colors and it looks great. You can also change the colors and how display within the MSI Center. I've tried a few of the settings, but the default works best for me. The touchpad is also good, it is smooth and doesn't hurt the tips of my fingers - this is a problem on HP laptops, but not Microsoft Laptops, Apple products, and MSI apparently. That's a big deal for me, as I had to buy finger protectors when I use the HP! Don't have to put that on for this MSI Stealth. 

Speaking of keyboard, the keys themselves are great and normal size and enough space between keys - unlike my HP where all the keys are so close together that if I’m typing too fast, my finger can hit 2 keys at the same time. Of course the reason for the space is due to the lack of a numeric keypad - which I usually want, but not at the risk of keys being too close to one another. 

The speakers are pretty decent, still not as loud as my favorite laptop, but at least i can hear game/sounds pretty clearly with my air purifier and a/c going on…I can’t say the same for other manufacturers.

After updating bios, Intel drivers, and NVidia drivers / and using the Game ready drivers, the NVidia control app can set the proper settings in each game for you, based on the capability of the computer. Using the recommendation from the NVidia app, Fortnite runs very smoothly in mid range graphic settings. Everything looks great and I can move very fast around, unlike my PS5. 

Fortnite also appears to run fine while you stream it AND capture the video at the same time. It's also very fast at post processing video editing of the streams.
 
So far, the only downside I've run into is the first USB-C port sometimes don't provide power to my PS5 controller. At first I thought it might be because I also connect a USB-C external monitor on the 2nd USB-C port, but that is not the case, as I can turn on the computer and the first USB-C still won't work. There is a fix though, when this happens, I plug it into the 2nd USB-C port, which always works, then plugging it back into the first USB-C and it's functional again. Minor annoyance, not sure what is going on, but seems to be specific to PS5 controllers (I've tried several), as plugging in the USB-C monitor always works on either port. 

Pros: 
Light weight in comparison to previous gaming laptops 
colorful backlit keys 
32GB of RAM 
240Hz OLED monitor 
Dedicated GPU 
Loud (but not too loud) speakers, I don't use a headset most of the time 
Proprietary power plug, leaving your other USB-C ports free 
You can also use 65W USB-C power if you forget / don't want to bring larger included power plug 

Cons: 
Proprietary power plug which is large and gets very hot! 
Not a touchscreen 
no numeric keypad 

Overall, the more I use it, the less I feel the need to turn on my other laptops, this will most likely become my main work/gaming machine.

reviews.title: A Stealthy Approach to Gaming and Productivity
reviews.content:
This computer keeps impressing me — the more I use it, the more I realize just how well‑rounded and thoughtfully put together the whole package really is. Let's get started!

The keyboard has a nice design with black key caps and transparent edges which light up via the RGB. The typing experience is just right giving the perfect amount of travel and feedback, while still being quiet and soft feeling. There is a slight amount of flex in the center of the keyboard but it’s very minimal and does not affect the feel or use of the keyboard at all. Honestly this keyboard might be one of the best I’ve used in a while, and I thoroughly enjoy typing on it. I’m using right now to type this review. 

The RGB for the keyboard is also very good. It’s a 4-zone RGB setup so you can choose 4 different colors yourself, or you can choose all solid so it’s the same color. There are also motion based lighting such as wave or breathing. It’s cool and I like it. The app that controls the lighting is located within MSI Center which comes on the laptop. It's named Mystic Light.

The screen is gorgeous. It’s the first thing you will notice once you power it on. Even going through Windows initial setup it’s apparent that the screen just looks great. Playing games with this screen is also amazing with the 240hz refresh rate and its ultra-low response time. It honestly makes any game just feel different and special. It’s probably my favorite feature of this laptop. It changes the feel of everything you do on it. The colors are vibrant and crystal clear. The bezels are super thin which also adds to the aesthetic.

The speakers are okay. Honestly, I was a little surprised for a laptop with this many high-end features to not have great speakers. I kept looking around and messing with different settings to try and get them to be better and that was only achieved with Nahimic software which is included but not apparent right away. You must search for it in the start menu and then you can tweak things much more to your liking. If you decide to use Nahimic make sure you keep the power button located at the top of the application on, as if you turn it off the sound will be hollow and just plain bad, so I highly recommend you keep this application/setting active. It still doesn’t compete with some brands but it’s also not the worst, just wish it was better.

The weight of the laptop is decent. It’s not the heaviest and not the lightest. I would say for the amount of power in this computer both CPU and GPU it’s kind of perfect. It feels solid when picking it up and carrying it, however I will mention there is some creaking in the chassis when you grab it in certain spots, and it could just be mine but sounds like there is a slight rattle coming from inside the computer. Not sure what it is but it’s only heard if you physically shake the computer. Overall, a good weight to performance ratio.

The look of the laptop is another understated feature. Besides the light up keyboard you would never know this was a gaming computer. Hence the name Stealth? Well, I do like the keyboard in an all-solid color and usually blue, its relaxing and cool looking. But they did do a really nice job with the aesthetics of the laptop. The materials appear to be all metal/aluminum, and it feels like a quality product. The bottom of the computer has large holes that have a finer screen metal mesh under them for the cooling system, and it just looks serious but at the same time Suttle. 

The cooling system on this laptop is another win. They did a good job on the cooling as when I’m playing a game with settings at high to ultra and the GPU is cranking away, the fans are at full throttle, but the laptop itself isn’t as hot as you would expect it to be. I’ve used other laptops that were so hot you couldn’t even touch it at certain spots. This laptop gets hot, just not scalding hot, as long as you have it on a solid surface so the bottom vents can move the air it needs. The bottom also has a bar protruding towards the rear which acts as a spacer to ensure the fans can pull air and it also angles the laptop slightly which makes for a more comfortable experience typing.

This laptop comes with a 5060 GPU and at first, I was expecting it to not perform as good, but it surprised me on just how smooth the gameplay was with AAA titles reaching 90 -120 FPS on High settings with DLSS turned on. Every game is different but honestly it surprised me for sure having the performed it does. The GPU also seems to top out at about +/- 99W of power at its highest performance, at least on the games I’ve tested which for a laptop this size, and the performance its putting out, and with the quality, it’s very good.

The trackpad is HUGE but feels very nice. My friend asked me if I ever hit the trackpad by accident when I’m typing and honestly it might have happened once or twice, but not enough to be a problem or even noticeable. I do agree it’s a very large trackpad and one might say, do you even need it that big? Again, it will come down to preference, but I think it’s very responsive and smooth and it just works so I have zero issues with it. It’s way better than others I have used so that’s that.

The proprietary charger is understandable due to the amount of power the GPU and the CPU can pull at any given time on top of charging requirements, but I do wish there was a TYPE-C method of main charging. There are two USB Type C ports on this computer and while they technically do support charging through PD, you will need the right USB cable in addition to a minimum 96 Watt Charger. This is from my testing where I had some good quality USB-C cables, and they weren’t charging with my 96W or 100W PD Chargers and I was confused because they have worked on every other computer I have. Come to find out it was the cables, I had beefy PD rated cable for 240W and that cable enabled the PD charging on the laptop. Sidenote is it will charge slower than the standard OEM charger of course due to the wattage difference.

The battery life has been pretty good. I have been taking the computer with me everyday and have been using it throughout the day sending emails, writing documents, watching videos, listening to music, and have been able to get through a full day without the battery exhausting on me. I am impressed with it because other gaming laptops I have used have less than desirable battery life to say the least. Another thing that impressed me was the ability to play games on just battery and still achieve decent performance, sometimes upwards of 70-80FPS. In my opinion, it strikes the perfect balance for everyday tasks and delivers an excellent gaming experience whenever you need it. 


*One issue WORTH mentioning:

At the initial time of writing this review I encountered an issue with “Failed Attestation” with COD BO7. I could not join normal multiplayer or ranked matches. I spent some time back and forth with both MSI and Activision. In the end I found a Windows repair tool called “DISM (Deployment Image Servicing and Management)”. 

There are command prompts you can run to fix corrupted files in the “Windows Component Store” which has ties to the trust chain for Attestation. After running the tool, I was able to resolve the issue with my computer not enrolling certificates with Azure that are needed, which Call of Duty checks to ensure your computer is compliant with certain security protocols. 

Besides COD not initially working I can report that the game now runs beautifully and I’m getting 80-100 FPS with Ultra settings and DLSS enabled. All the other games I have played have run without issue, have great performance and are very enjoyable. This computer has a lot of power for such a slim form factor and best of all using it for normal school/work tasks has also performed very well. I am easily getting a full day of battery with the power plan set on “Balanced” which is important and a good feature for a gaming laptop. You can be productive during the day and then game in your spare time. I look forward to taking this laptop with me daily as it becomes my new go to device for fun and work.

Highly recommend it to anyone that is looking for a great gaming computer that also serves as a day-to-day productivity machine.

reviews.title: An Immediate Visual Upgrade to Any Game
reviews.content:
[PROS]

Eye Candy: The Stealth 16 AI+ is a vibrant and overall gorgeous display. Being an OLED panel already produces the inky blacks, but the DisplayHDR600 makes colors pop. This pairing of visual technologies make the laptop suitable for gaming as well as media work.

Limit Pushing: I do find myself impressed in the ways that an 8GB GPU can be pushed when gaming. DLSS allows me to squeeze out extra frames to get or close to 60fps in newer titles, but frame generation puts me over the top. Despite the controversy around FG, my gameplay experience was fluid, input lag wasn't noticeable, and I failed to observe any visual oddities.

Powerful and Customizable Laptop: Just about everything outside of the gaming specs is A1. The Intel Ultra 9 processor 386H and 32GB RAM combo makes this a multitasking monster. I'm able to use multiple programs in unison and switch among applications with relative ease. The included 1TB SSD provides ample storage, and allows me to install a healthy amount of games. What makes this laptop even greater is there an extra SSD slot. I've already upgraded so now I have a total of 4TB. Also, there are 2 RAM sticks included so dual channel mode is already enabled.

[CONS]

Not Gaming Future Proof: The biggest thing that nags me about this laptop is the GPU. No matter the generation or architecture, a 8GB VRAM graphics card will be obsolete sooner rather than later for major AAA games. If this laptop is used for esports, cozy titles, AA games, or anything before 2020 then using the high graphical preset is fine in most scenarios. The Stealth 16 would even be overkill. However, many post-pandemic AAA titles are demanding and require playing using upscaling along with optimized settings. Reducing the resolution would help, but defeats the purpose of playing on such a beautiful and sharp display. 

[CONCLUSION]

Overall, the Stealth 16 AI+ is an amazing device with 1 slight drawback depending on the type of gamer you are. Personally, it works well me given that I have a huge backlog that would take me a couple of years to complete. Yet, it can still provide a wonderful experience for the average gamer, and its very mighty in all other areas. I would highly recommend it.

reviews.title: Beautiful display. Great Performance. Thin + Light
reviews.content:
TLDR; This laptop has a lot to like, not only with some standout features, but also with a lot of small things here and there that add to the total package. It looks great, performs very well, and even at its price point, provides very good value; both on its own, and especially when compared to others in the space.
Pros:
-	“Compact” design for a gaming laptop
-	OLED display with 240Hz refresh rate that while glossy handles reflections well
-	Performance / Specs (386H CPU, 32GB RAM, 1 TB SSD storage, RTX5060 GPU)
-	2 slots for both RAM and SSD for upgradeability
-	Port selection
-	Quality keyboard
-	Good battery life charging speed
-	Solid sound with up-firing speakers
Cons:
-	Port placement
-	Trackpad, while large, is not the best
-	Charging brick is large, cable is proprietary, and USB charging requires some work
-	Webcam is average, both in picture and sound

The first thing I noticed with this laptop was the size, weight, and build. With gaming laptops, they often tend towards the “desktop replacement” side of things, yet I found this to be rather thin, light, and somewhat compact. Easy to “one-hand” it, and easily one of the lightest gaming laptops I have used. It is nice to see in a system with a dedicated video card. Beyond that, I really like the build. Rounded edges, solid, and with a good feel in the hand. The is some minimal give here and there, but nothing really to note. Good materials choices, although the bottom lacks some of the premium feel (is great for air intake though). As for the look, I like it. It is understated, which, given the name makes sense. No flashy exterior RGB, just a small logo in the bottom corner and some etched line detail on the case. Honestly, it is what I am looking for. If anything, I would like even less, but that is just me. I would really like this completely blacked out. Regardless, it is modern, clean, and subtle. It can easily fit in a professional environment if need be.

The display is fantastic. Great size, good resolution, OLED, and 240Hz refresh rate. Colors are vibrant and accurate, blacks are OLED inky, and there is defined contrast. It is bright, although not the brightest. Clarity is top notch, with everything from games, video, and images to text being crisp and clear. Response times are essentially instantaneous. It is glossy, but there must be some anti-reflective work at play, as reflections are not much of an issue. I usually prefer matte, or texture, but this is done well.

As much as I like the build and display, I think where this laptop really shines is in the specs. Yes, there are machines with more, but that is reflected in the price. Here, I think the hardware is a nice blend of performance, cost, efficiency, and upgradeability. I think the CPU was a great choice. The 386H has 3 sets of cores. Performance. Efficiency. Low Power Efficiency. This gives you performance but also better battery life. The 1TB SSD is good, and while more is always better, it works here (more on that later). The 32GB of DDR5 RAM is really nice to see, especially given the market out there right now.  Given todays needs, I am glad to not have concerns right at purchase. The 5060 Is good for me. Again, yes, some may want more, but I am happy with it and what it does for me.

All of that said, while I do really like the hardware mix, what I really like and think they nailed is upgradeability. There are 2 RAM slots, and while they are both populated, it can max out at 128GB. There are also 2 PCIe4 SSD slots, with one bring free at purchase. This is seemingly more uncommon these days, but something that is so important to me personally, and especially given the costs out there right now. It prices ever go down you can add to this system down the road, or, as I am doing, bringing some storage forward from a previous system. That flexibility and future proofing is something I really appreciate. Given the initial outlay, I like anything that can help me extend the life of this machine. You can also easily replace the battery and WiFi card if ever needed.

Port selection is solid. 2 Thunderbolt 4 USB-C ports, 2 USB-A ports (3.2 gen 2), an HDMI 2.1 interface, a headphone multi-jack, and a 2.5gbps hardwired ethernet jack (a nice add). I think everyone should be covered and happy here. Not including a SD card reader is slight miss, and something to note. As much as I like the port choices, I do not like their placement. Both USB-C and the charging port (more on that later) are on the left side. I really would have liked the USB-C being split between sides which makes it more convenient for charging. Additionally, having the working ports (ethernet, HDMI, a USB-A, and audio jack) on the right side makes it kind of a mess by the mouse if you are connected there. Perhaps a personal thing, but I would have preferred all of this flipped.

I like the keyboard. Scissor switches, centered, “mostly” full size arrow keys, and with good key travel. It is responsive, feels nice to type with, is thumpy, and I found it quick to get used to. There is also fingerprint reader in the power key. It generally is a MacBook look and layout. The track pad is, well, good. It is large, and again centered, which I like, but has some give and doesn’t have the best feel in use. There are some nice gestures that can be used, but they haven’t been the most accurate. Not a dealbreaker, as I often will be using a mouse, and it is good, but just something to know going in.

Sound is surprisingly good. The up-firing speakers definitely help, as do the 2 woofers. It is not amazing, but good. It gets loud, there is some low end, and there is not much distortion until you get close to maxxing out volume. This could always be better, but I like it and have no complaints. The webcam is about average. You should have no problem using it for calls or meetings, but the picture, while ok, has color issues and some things look blown out. The mic is about the same. It all works, so no worries, but don’t look for cinematic quality. There is a manual privacy shield which is nice to see and frankly should be the standard.

Battery life has been quite good for me. I was perhaps expecting a bit more given the CPU choice, but I have no complaints. I am roughly getting rated numbers. In daily use, there is no concern, and gaming, well, that is done plugged in. I don’t think it will be an issue going forward. Charging is quick, and you can use the brick or USB-C. That said, the brick is somewhat large and the connection is proprietary. There is PD charging and delivery, but that is capped at 100W (versus 240W on the brick) and you will want to make sure you have a proper brick and cable. Some good and some bad here, but not really an issue and given 240W is the max thunderbolt is rated for, I see why they went this way.

Performance-wise, I could not be happier. Performance is very good. Zero issues in the with my day-to-day, office tasks, messaging, video, content consumption, content creation, or imaging work. Even my “tab problem,” goes unnoticed. Battery drain is minimal. Games, which is what most people are probably curious about, were much of the same. Again, it is not a 5080, but games are smooth, I am getting good frame rates and haven’t seen much, if any, dropping or tearing. I do tweak some settings to my liking here and there, but all in all I am very pleased. All of this has been with good temperatures and being largely quiet (it does run a little hot in extreme mode). Air intake is via the bottom and vents from the bottom, back, and from two small slits on the top of the chassis. The laptop is silent unless really being pushed, and when the fans do start spinning, it is, yes, noticeable, but not that bad and I think most would be fine with it.

Well, not sure why I wrote a literal book to get here, but I do very much like this laptop. It is a good size, yet somewhat compact, is well built, and has a gorgeous display. It has solid battery-life, I like how it is spec’d out and it performs very well. Lastly, it has wonderful upgradability, which is a big selling point for me. While there are some things that I wish they had done differently, I think those things are outweighed by all that you get here. Yes, it all comes at a premium price point, but I truly think there is value here on its own, and especially when compared to others across the space. It’s a good machine and I think most would be happy with it.

reviews.title: Power and Style
reviews.content:
MSI’s flagship Stealth gaming and productivity laptops have been refreshed with the latest Intel Ultra 3rd generation processors, combined with a new external shell design and other features. This model comes well equipped with an Ultra 9, 32GB of DDR5 memory, 1TB of storage, and an Nvidia RTX 5060 GPU. Does this generation live up to the premium price tag, and does the mid range GPU hold it back? Let’s take a look and find out.

In the box, you’ll find the laptop, some basic documentation, and the power supply. The laptop itself is covered in a nice sleeve and there is a microfiber protective fabric sheet between the keyboard and the display to keep your new laptop in perfect condition during shipping. The microfiber cloth is nice enough to keep with the laptop to clean the screen and protect it during travel. The box and packaging appear to be completely recyclable. This system comes with a powerful, 240W power supply to fully power the system and it uses a proprietary connection. For the output of the power supply, it isn’t as huge as some are. It’s fairly thin and uses a standard PC power cable for the cable that goes to the wall, meaning replacements or different lengths are easy to find. You can provide up to 100W of power via power delivery using USB-C, which will provide enough power for most productivity tasks, but will not allow the system to run at full tilt gaming mode with the CPU and GPU running.

For connectivity, the system comes decently equipped with two Thunderbolt 4 USB-C ports, two USB-A ports, an HDMI 2.1 interface, a headphone multijack, and a 2.5gbps hardwired ethernet jack. The ethernet jack is NOT the kind that flips open to expand, which is nice as that is a common failure point. One slightly annoying thing is that both thunderbolt ports are on the left side, so if you have a setup that connects to a dock or other peripherals on the right side, you’ll need to route the cables around the back of the laptop, avoiding the power connector. Internally, this system is refreshingly accessible and upgradeable. Flip it over, remove the 7 screws (4 are obvious on the corners and three are hidden in the bottom grille), and gently pop off the bottom panel from the back corners. What you will find inside is an open standard sized SSD expansion slot, the wifi card, the battery, and something increasingly rare, even on gaming laptops – two removeable SODIMM DDR5 RAM sticks under some heatsinks. This allows the user to upgrade or replace the memory instead of using fully integrated, soldered on RAM like many systems use now. This system already is loaded with 32GB of memory, but it’s nice to know that you can expand or upgrade the capacity if you need to. Since I had it open, I did install a second 1TB SSD to give me plenty of space for larger games.

Overall, this system exudes subtle sophistication with only faint nods to gaming. This system will fit in either doing professional content creation or playing games. The touchpad is gigantic, allowing for a lot of accuracy when a mouse isn’t in your bag. The keyboard is nice with a good feel and a coating that is supposed to resist sheen and oils. The speakers are, for a laptop, decent. They still lack bass but provide a clear sound that avoids the “tinny” sound that many laptops have.

The screen is an immediate highlight. With a native 2560x1600 resolution, HDR 600 certification, and a screaming fast 240hz refresh on an OLED panel, this display is better than most monitors people have. Everything is crisp and clear, and videos look great on it. MSI says it features Corning glass for long term durability and it does a good job rejecting glare even with a glossy finish.

After the usual Windows 11 setup, the system is ready to go. With the CPU and GPU in this model, you have the ability to turn on all of the Copilot+ features. I did some driver and BIOS upgrades, and also installed all of the modules on MSI Center to check them out. Using MSI center, I was able to set the keyboard’s 4 lighting zones and a few other system parameters. This laptop also supports both fingerprint and face recognition for Windows Hello, using passkeys, etc.

Finally, it’s time to really put this thing through its paces. Many gamers will notice that this model is equipped with the RTX 5060, which is a respectable but not the highest end graphics card. And, as a gamer, I had some reservations about the GPU after some of the mixed press it got at release. After playing several games on this laptop, it is more than adequate for all but the most demanding or discerning gamers on the native display. If you plan on using this laptop as a desktop replacement and connecting it to a high refresh rate external monitor, you may want to look for the models with a more performant GPU, but the price jumps up into a truly incredible price point, and still has the limitations of a laptop, which include fan noise. This laptop, fully spun up, is not the loudest on the planet (partially due to the thermal system being designed to handle up to a 5080 and only needing to cool a 5060), but it does make some air noise when gaming.

Doing basic productivity tasks, web browsing, or watching movies, this system just sips the 90 watt-hour battery. It will go for hours doing basic work and can easily last “all day” doing those kinds of tasks.

Overall, if you are a creator or a gamer who wants a well equipped laptop in a sleek, well built, and portable package, this is one you should take a look at. The display is fantastic, the CPU can rip through just about anything thrown at it, and the GPU, while not the highest end part, is a good balance of budget, performance, and power usage.

reviews.title: Beautiful OLED screen and cool when gaming.
reviews.content:
Pros:
-240Hz OLED Display
-Strong study frame
-Quiet cooling 
-Smooth keys, and large touchpad

Cons:
-Battery life drains fast
-Big power brick 

A nice gaming laptop with a vibrant high refresh rate OLED display. It has a good strong build quality. With the RTX5060 and 32GB of Ram, it’s able to deliver on a good gaming experience while being a well balanced and quiet laptop. The battery life doesn’t last that long, and it has a big power brick that makes it less portable.

The available ports are 2x USB Type A, 2x Thunderbolt 4/USB Type C, an HDMI 2.1 (up to 8K 60Hz), an Ethernet Port, and a headphone jack. It’s lacking a micro SD Card that’s usually available in other laptops, which is sometimes needed even if on rare occasions. 

Setup was a bit of a drag though, it took about 30-40 minutes before all updates completed and I could use the laptop. It's mostly all Windows issues, but kind of felt like they had a much older instance installed. There was also a trial of Norton antivirus loaded, which is good to start off - but when I installed my other AV, it caused some sort of network driver conflict and I had to restart the driver to browse the web properly (and of course, uninstalling Norton). 
 
The 1440p OLED display is beautiful, vibrant and bright, and offers good contrast. It’s a clear difference over the LCD screen of my previous laptop. It goes up to 240Hz for smooth gameplay, but achieving that level of refresh rate with moderate games is unlikely due to the limited capability of the 5060. 

The RGB keyboard looks pleasing, and the keys click very smoothly and quietly while still giving a tactile feel. The touch pad is nice and big, making it easy to navigate with. This will help when I work or take notes during any calls I might take on this laptop.  

One drawback is the power brick. It’s on the bigger side, so it's not quite as portable, and it has a square shaped connector which could potentially be easier to damage or replace. It’s a little cumbersome and I don't know how much traveling I'll end up doing with this laptop, since I often have to travel with a work laptop as well. I'm enjoying using it around the house and getting to play games out of my office though, so it serves its purpose.

I don’t really play the most demanding games so I doubt I fully pushed the laptop to the fullest, but the games I did played performed well. I tried Magic The Gathering Arena, which is a big memory hog. It loaded smoothly and had no issues at all. The laptop did not have to push the fans on much, unlike my older rig. Next I loaded up Diablo 4, which took a couple minutes to sync properly and was choppy upon the first boot, but the gameplay smoothed out after a couple minutes. The ventilation was good, utilizing the larger size to keep the laptop cool and the fans quiet. It kept the laptop’s body from heating up and allowing a more comfortable gaming experience.

The battery life isn’t great but not uncommon for gaming laptops. It drained fast even while just browsing, and didn’t last long during gaming.

Overall, I'm very pleased with this laptop and would highly recommend it to a fellow gamer. Gaming on it was a good experience with the OLED screen being the stand out. It has all the ports you would expect with the exception of the SD Card slot. It does have a big power brick with a proprietary connection which may be an issue.

reviews.title: The display really makes this system stand out!
reviews.content:
The MSI Stealth 16+ AI is a well-built gaming system with an EXCEPTIONAL display!

I was immediately impressed by how vibrant the MSI logo looked when I first booted the system. Having owned many gaming laptops, this display, right out of the box, is by far the most vibrant and color accurate that I have experienced. Games and Movies felt extremely smooth with no noticeable motion blur, jitter, or screen tearing. Colors were vibrant and crisp, and the high contract ratio ensured darker scenes remained well defined. The audio quality is also quite good, not great, but for a laptop I'm quite pleased. Quality remained consistent, at high volumes and the speakers offer a decent amount of bass response.  Overall, gaming on this system has been very enjoyable. 

Unlike other gaming laptops MSI - Stealth 16 AI+ stays cool under heavy load. I've been able to easily game with the laptop resting directly on my lap without noticeable discomfort. With other systems I've needed a solid barrier to prevent burns.  

The keyboard is smooth and responsive. It offers the perfect balance between smoothness and tactile feedback. There is very little flex in the display, and the hinges hold the display perfectly in place, even while moving the system around. There are a few quirks in the design that I'll mention, but do not detract from my 5-Star rating. The first being the oversized trackpad. Large trackpads are nice, when palm rejection works well, which in a few cases I noticed my cursor drifting unexpectedly. The other and probably my biggest dislike of this laptop; the charging cable.  The charging cable, specifically the connection point, resembles a USB dongle and sticks out quite far from the system. My fear is that overtime, one wrong move, will cause it to break off. There are two PD charging ports, however during my testing, I found PD charging to be inconsistent. When connected to a 100W PD charger, the laptop would rapidly cycle between charge and battery. My hope is that a future firmware update will resolve this issue.  Quirks aside, the system is well-built, sturdy, and light weight, which is often not the case for gaming systems of this caliber. 

In all, the MSI - Stealth 16 AI+ 16" 2.5K 240Hz OLED Gaming Laptop Intel Core U9-386H - NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 - 32GB Memory -1TB Storage is a great system, perfect for both work, school, and play. I would happily, and without hesitation, recommend this system to a friend. 

Pros:
-OLED display with 240Hz refresh rate and 16:10 aspect ratio
-32GB Ram / 1TB storage / RTX 5060
-Smooth Keyboard - Smooth, responsive, tactile response. 
-Excellent battery life
-Thermal management - Stays cool to touch, even under heavy load / Quiet Fans.
-Great sound, decent bass response. No noticeable distortion at high volumes. 

Cons:
-Oversized track pad, inconsistent palm rejection - May be fixed with firmware update. 
-Large connector on charge cable, protrudes quite far - may break in future.
-PD charging inconsistent - May be fixed with firmware update.

reviews.title: Amazing OLED Screen, Great for Gaming
reviews.content:
My time with the MSI Stealth 16 AI+ has been great so far, minus the initial unboxing. Im happy to say it's exceeded my expectations.

After unboxing, the first thing I noticed was a piece at the back of the base that was hanging off and not properly clicked in place. This was maybe something overlooked by quality control?. Or could of happened during shipment. Luckily, it was easy to snap back into place. I've included a picture for reference. Not the end of the world, but still worth mentioning.

After the initial setup, I was blown away by the gorgeous OLED display, this is my first laptop with one. The colors are vibrant and details don't get drowned out by darker areas like non OLED panels. The contrast is amazing too and it gets very bright. The 240Hz refresh rate makes everything feel super smooth. From gaming to movies, to normal browsing and switching windows, the 16 inch display always looks sharp. Seriously, the display is probably my favorite feature.

This laptop feels well built too, and I like the subtle charcoal color. The classic msi logo is neat but doesn't look out of place either. The keyboard is comfortable to type on with nice spacing between the keys. The trackpad is responsive and huge with plenty of room for righties or lefties. There's an impressive amount of ports and connectivity options as well. The Ethernet port, was a welcome surprise to see that they made an effort to include. I prefer to be hardwired since my wifi can be spotty sometimes. Speakers sound great too and don't lose quality at higher volumes. The fans are noticeable when the system is under heavier load, but they aren't distracting. That's to be expected from a laptop with this level of performance, especially during more demanding games.

Speaking of performance, it has been excellent. The Intel Core U9 processor runs like butter. This bad boy has a RTX 5060 and 32GB of RAM and has handled everything I've thrown at it. Most games run smoothly at high settings, like call of duty and fortnite. I've also used it for video editing, streaming and reading manga online, without any noticeable hiccups. Switching between multiple applications is effortless and storage is fast with room for expansion.

I really appreciate the design overall. It has a clean look, instead of the usual flashy gaming laptop design and way less bulky too. Its thin enough to carry around comfortably whether you're using it for work or school. Even while traveling, it's small enough to fit in almost any bag comfortably. Don't worry about over heating because the cooling system does a great job of keeping temperatures under control. During longer gaming sessions, you can monitor the diagnostics and even adjust on the fly. Having it rest on my legs while I'm bed, it does get a little warm but not unbearable.

Battery life has been better than I expected for a gaming laptop during everyday tasks like web browsing, watching videos, and working on documents. For gaming, I still keep it plugged in to get the best performance, which is when you'll hear fans cranking up, but this isn't an issue.

Lastly, if you're in the market for a gaming laptop that feels premium but takes up little space, I think the MSI Stealth 16 AI+ is an excellent choice. The build quality is top notch and that OLED panel is a huge selling point for me. It's an investment, but based on my experience so far, it's been well worth it. Definitely a keeper.

reviews.title: MSI VECTOR 16 HX
reviews.content:
I’ve been extremely impressed with my MSI Vector 16 HX AI. After gaming and using it daily, I can confidently say this thing is a beast.

My configuration has the Intel Core Ultra 9 275HX, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5080, 16GB RAM, 1TB SSD, and 16-inch QHD+ 240Hz display. The specs are impressive, but using it is where it shines.

Performance is incredible. Games run smoothly, the RTX 5080 delivers plenty of power, and the high-refresh-rate display feels responsive. At 240Hz, fast-paced games look sharp and fluid.

The display is one of my favorite features. Its size, QHD+ resolution, and 240Hz refresh rate balance image quality with competitive gaming performance perfectly.

The Vector also works as a desktop replacement. I can connect multiple monitors and peripherals at home, then unplug and take the same performance with me.

The RTX 5080 paired with the Core Ultra 9 means I rarely compromise on settings. The overall design is powerful without being over-the-top, making it suitable for gaming, work, everyday tasks, and creative applications.

It isn’t lightweight, but that’s not why I bought it. You’re getting serious desktop-class gaming capability in a portable system.

The only upgrade I may consider is more RAM. With hardware this powerful, 16GB could eventually limit heavier multitasking.

Overall, the MSI Vector 16 HX AI exceeded my expectations. It’s fast, powerful, smooth, flexible, and equipped with an awesome display.

If you’re considering the Core Ultra 9 and RTX 5080 configuration, yes, it absolutely feels premium.

I love this laptop and would buy it again without hesitation.

10/10 — an absolute powerhouse.

reviews.title: Beautiful & Blazing fast!
reviews.content: I am so happy with this purchase. I was lucky enough to see an ad for this laptop when it was still $1,299 and, boy, am I glad I pulled the trigger on this one, especially since the price has since risen to $1,999. I was specifically looking for a thin and light laptop with decent RAM capacity and, more specifically, LPDDR5X. The Low Power Double Data Rate memory is soldered directly on the board, very close to the processor, so it's blazing fast, and this thing has 32GB, which is more than enough for most people, even for gaming. When I researched LPDDR5X and discovered that the max transfer speed was 8533MT/s, I assumed that was just a theoretical upper limit. But Windows Task manager and the Performance tab reflect that, and I ran AIDA64 benchmarks immediately after receiving it, and it's quite fast, with a sustained read speed of 87808 MB/s and latency of 95.3 ns. AIDA64 GPGPU Benchmark showed single-precision FLOPS of 3974 and memory copy of 70.8 GB/s. These aren't anywhere near discreet GPU numbers in a desktop gaming rig, but it's pretty darned good for a shared-memory iGPU. I decided to try some light gaming, and installed Steam and Final Fantasy XIV. I was absolutely flabbergasted when it ran the game perfectly with most settings maxed out. If you do plan on gaming with this laptop, keep in mind that, as a thin and light laptop with an integrated GPU it's not meant to run AAA games. That being said, it does have 2 USB-C/Thunderbolt 4 ports, so you could (and plenty of people have) run it with an external GPU to get something approximating a desktop gaming experience. Speaking of I/O, I'm totally satisfied with what is included; 2 Thunderbolt ports, HDMI, only a single USB-A slot, a Micro SD card reader (which I will get plenty of use out of, transferring print files to a Bambu 3D printer), and, of course, WiFi and Bluetooth. The OLED screen has some of the richest color and deepest blacks I have seen in a laptop, but the screen is very glossy and tends to throw off a lot of glare in dark conditions or subdued ambient light. If you're watching YouTube or streaming in a dark room, you'll definitely see yourself reflected on screen. The battery is great, too. I had heard in a video somewhere that they estimated it could continuously display video for up to 23 hours on a single charge, depending on the power management settings. And let's talk about this lid. Wow. Each one is handcrafted by Japanese lacquerware artisans with a version of Hokusai's Great Wave Off Kanagawa, which anyone who is familiar with Japanese art or, more specifically, woodblock prints, will immediately recognize. It is absolutely beautiful, but it is also a fingerprint magnet, and they REALLY show up, so be prepared to constantly buff the lid with the microfiber cloth sandwiched between the keyboard and the screen. Everything about this laptop is a work of art. The box is beautiful, too, and opens in such a way that it tilts the back of the laptop up out of the box to make it very easy to remove carefully. It includes a pretty little mouse with similar lacquerware artistry, but I'm not sure if it's actual lacquerware; I left it in the box, along with the cool badge holder and the extended mousepad/deskpad with matching art. The bundled laptop sleeve is nothing fancy. It has a nice soft, velvety texture to it, but ZERO padding, so it's not something I will be using regularly. Instead, I will probably opt for one of the Thule hard-shell cases. I feel like this is one of those rare instances where an electronic device will continue to retain some value after purchase. Each one is numbered, but I'm not sure what the production runs are all about. Mine is numbered XXX/700 A, so perhaps there are several production runs (A, B, C, etc.), each 700, because I can't imagine they will only ever make 700 of these. MSI's own website mentions that it comes with "up to Intel® Core™ Ultra 9 processor(Series 2)", but I have only seen this version. That being said, I can't imagine there would be a noticeable difference in performance between the two specs. This thing is a work of art, inside and out, and I can't imagine anyone being unhappy after purchasing one. If you're in the market for a thin and light laptop, and your budget is flexible enough, go for it. This is probably the absolute best electronic device purchase I have ever made.

reviews.title: Amazing machine, both looks and function
reviews.content:
First off, you get some cool matching accessories: mousepad, mouse, luggage tag, etc. It's a nice inclusion which may not be obvious from the description.

The laptop itself looks amazing. This isn't just some sticker on the lid or whatever, it's actually got texture to it and appears to be lacquered. It actually looks better in person than the pictures.

Performance-wise, this machine is also top notch. It is powerful, has a great OLED display, nice port selection, and is extremely light. Battery lasts an incredible amount of time too - about 10 hrs of mixed use in my experience. It has an IR camera for Windows Hello, and the webcam (which is pretty decent) has a physical shutter built in.

RAM is not upgradeable, but it ships with 32GB which should be plenty for most. The SSD can be swapped (1 slot only). I dropped in a 2TB 970 EVO I had from a previous machine and, after some fumbling with drivers, got a clean Windows install up. Note on that: you should probably download the drivers from MSI's site to a USB beforehand if this is your only device and you want to do the same. 

I have only two minor complaints: the speakers aren't great, and the machine is a huge fingerprint magnet. 

With regards to the speakers, they do get loud but don't sound great. Bass in particular is lacking. This isn't a big deal for me as I don't usually use this for media, but others may find it a bigger problem.

The keys have that same lacquered finish as the lid, but both will show fingerprint marks very easily... and it's kind of hard to avoid touching either of those parts (especially the keys!) Let's just say there's a good reason they included a big microfiber cloth.

The only other thing to note is the top of the lid is a bit squishy. I wouldn't put anything heavy on it, but then again you probably wouldn't want to anyway as it might damage that super nice art on it.

Overall, I really like this device, though I'll admit a lot of it is just how nice it looks.

reviews.content: This is my first gamimg laptop and it is thin! It is quiet and when it started to push i turned on my cooling stand and it almost instantly got quiet again. Graphics and screen are amazing!! It is costly, but not as bad as the Asus and pulls similar FPS. So far so good!

reviews.title: A very good buy for work and play.
reviews.content:
I ordered this laptop for two reasons: work and gaming.  On the work end, Im able to write reports, complete tasks, and participate in virtual office meetings.  On the gaming end, games that were difficult, even impossible to play (FFXVI, EU5, Visions of Mana, Valkyrie Elysium, Star Ocean: The Divine Force, Stranger of Paradise: FF Origins, Anno 117) on my old laptop now all play seamlessly.
I would definitely recommend this laptop for all purposes.

reviews.title: The more practical Thin and light
reviews.content: From my experience so far MSI definitely has thrown a good pitch this year for thin & lights as they massively overhauled it for the better. Has everything i need for it and the practicality you would find on thicker laptops. My only gripe would be port positioning and the rattly track pad which makes it feel a little cheap. Overall if you can find it at a good price its well worth, just make sure you update the software ASAP.

reviews.title: Worth the price
reviews.content:
I love this laptop. I’m using it as a desktop replacement, for gaming and general computer stuff. It’s solidly built with a nice, minimalist design that doesn’t scream “gamer.”  The OLED screen is absolutely stunning, and it easily handles new (2026) games at max settings. If anything, the specs are overkill for what I actually need, but I wanted a future-proof machine. 

Compared to other laptops with these kinds of specs, it’s light and portable, and the fan is relatively quiet. The keyboard is excellent - satisfyingly clicky without that gummy feeling you get from a lot of gaming laptops. The undercarriage gets a little toasty while running GPU intensive games, so don’t plan on using it directly on your lap. It’s expensive, yes, but not compared to similar models from other makers. 

All in all, this laptop is one of the best I’ve ever owned

reviews.title: Excellent fast professional laptop good for gaming
reviews.content: Purchased this three weeks ago and it has been a delight to use. Ordered online and picked up at store. I wanted an all-round laptop good for coding, AI development, general office use, plus gaming. I chose this because it is one of the few choices with Windows Hello webcam and fingerprint reader, Intel Ultra 9, Nvidia 5080, and is upgradeable to 64 GB RAM. OLED screen is excellent. Port selection also very good, so I don't need a docking station. Has single 2 TB drive, despite the current Best Buy features section saying 1 TB. Overall, I'm very happy.

reviews.title: MSI nailed it this year!
reviews.content:
It’s safe to say MSI absolutely knocked it out of the park with the 2026 Stealth 16 AI+. I’ve been in the market for a new laptop for a few months now, weighing a few different options like the Zephyrus G16 and the Razer Blade 16. I wanted something sleek, portable, and highly capable of handling both gaming and content creation. I can confidently say the Stealth 16 AI+ checks every single box.

If you’re currently cross-shopping other laptops like the G16, I highly recommend giving this one a shot. For starters, it’s about $400 cheaper while offering double the storage and upgradeable RAM. Sure, the GPU power (TGP) is a bit lower than the G16, but you really have to ask yourself if a slight performance bump is worth an extra $400. For me, gaming performance has been fantastic, it handles everything from Lego Batman to Forza Horizon 6 like a champ. The build quality is solid, it looks incredibly clean, and it's exactly what I was looking for.

The only catch: My first unit arrived with a rattling trackpad and a creaky hinge. I exchanged it, and the replacement unit is absolutely rock solid.

If you’re looking for a powerful, “stealthy” laptop for gaming, content creation, and daily work, you should definitely take a look at this one.
